hero.title: Constitutional Accuracy Checks
hero.description: Constitutional Accuracy Checks form the cornerstone of judicial review, legislative validation, and administrative accountability in India. For Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC aspirants, mastering this topic is vital for drafting rigorous essays on rule of law, judicial activism, and separation of powers.

timeline.title: Evolution of Constitutional Checks and Judicial Review
timeline.description: Key historical milestones defining the boundaries between legislature, executive, and judiciary in India.

cards.details: Supremacy of Parliament affirmed in early cases like Shankari Prasad (1951) and Sajjan Singh (1965) regarding Fundamental Rights amendment.
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala established that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure of the Constitution.
Introduction of Public Interest Litigation (PIL) by Justice P.N. Bhagwati, expanding locus standi and enforcing constitutional rights for marginalized groups.
Supreme Court struck down the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act and NJAC Act, upholding judicial primacy in judge appointments under the Collegium system.

items.question: Which constitutional article explicitly empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
items.answer: Article 32 (Dr. B.R. Ambedkar termed it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution).

items.question: In which landmark case was the 'Basic Structure Doctrine' propounded?
items.answer: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973).

items.question: Which article mandates the separation of judiciary from the executive?
Who is empowered to audit the accounts of the Union and State governments under Article 149?
items.answer: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG).

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Confusing Article 32 and Article 226 Jurisdiction: Aspirants often think High Court writ jurisdiction under Article 226 is narrower than Supreme Court under Article 32. In reality, High Court's writ jurisdiction is wider as it covers both Fundamental Rights and 'other purposes'.

Misinterpreting Judicial Review Scope: Judicial review in India applies to both legislative enactments and executive actions, unlike the US where it originated mainly for laws. Ensure you distinguish between American 'due process of law' and Indian 'procedure established by law'.

deepDive.title: Constitutional Accuracy Checks Core Study Notes
deepDive.description: Constitutional Accuracy Checks form the cornerstone of judicial review, legislative validation, and administrative accountability in India. For Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC aspirants, mastering this topic is vital for drafting rigorous essays on rule of law, judicial activism, and separation of powers.

sections.title: Constitutional Framework & Fundamental Doctrines
sections.content:
The Indian Constitution incorporates explicit and implicit checks and balances to prevent authoritarianism and maintain federal equilibrium.

  • Article 13 and Judicial Review: Declares that all laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights shall be void, empowering courts to perform constitutional accuracy checks.
  • Basic Structure Doctrine: An unwritten yardstick derived from Kesavananda Bharati (1973) comprising secularism, federalism, judicial review, and parliamentary democracy.
  • Separation of Powers (Article 50): Directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State.
  • Doctrine of Pith and Substance: Used by courts to examine the true nature and character of legislation to determine if it falls within the legislative competence of the respective List (VII Schedule).

sections.title: Legislative Oversight & Executive Accountability
sections.content:
Parliamentary control mechanisms ensure that executive actions remain within constitutional limits and fiscal propriety is maintained.

  • Parliamentary Committees: Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Estimates Committee, and Committee on Subordinate Legislation scrutinize delegated legislation and government expenditure.
  • Question Hour and Zero Hour: Vital parliamentary instruments allowing MPs to extract information from ministers and keep administrative machinery on check.
  • Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG - Art 148): Acts as the guardian of the public purse, conducting constitutional accuracy checks on financial transactions of Union and State governments.

sections.title: Judicial Reforms and Contemporary Challenges
sections.content:
Ensuring constitutional accuracy requires addressing structural delays, judicial backlog, and maintaining institutional credibility.

  • Pendency and Case Backlog: Over 5 crore cases pending across Indian courts undermine the fundamental right to speedy trial under Article 21.
  • Subordinate Judiciary Strengthening: National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms focuses on infrastructure upgrades and digital courts (e-Courts project phase III).
  • Judicial Overreach Debates: Balancing judicial activism with judicial restraint to prevent encroachment into executive and legislative domains.

sections.title: Socio-Economic & Federal Governance Checks
sections.content:
Constitutional accuracy also extends to distributive justice, federal cooperation, and localized governance integrity under Panchayats and Municipalities.

  • Directive Principles (Part IV): Serve as fundamental benchmarks for socio-economic justice, tested by courts for welfare policy alignment (e.g., Article 39(b) and (c)).
  • Cooperative Federalism (Art 246): Union and State lists division audited through judicial interpretation to prevent encroachment on regional legislative sovereignty.
  • Local Self-Governance (73rd & 74th Amendments): State Finance Commissions and District Planning Committees ensure decentralization accuracy and resource devolution.
